0.why: seed.cpp:89 getVoltage() * 10000 cast to unsigned, channel 0 only; unpatched it keeps currentSeed, set once at seed.cpp:83
seed.cpp:100 setChannels(16); values from uniform_real_distribution{0, 10} at seed.cpp:85

1.why: seed.cpp:110 setVoltage with no channel argument

comment: The unpatched seed is not random. seed.cpp:83 initialises currentSeed from a default-constructed std::mt19937, which has a fixed default seed, so every Seed module with an empty Seed jack produces the same sixteen voltages on every machine and at every launch; the readme says a random seed is used. The seed voltage is multiplied by 10000 and cast to unsigned int, so what a negative seed voltage does depends on the platform's float-to-unsigned conversion and was not tested here.
